title: Improve residency enforcement error messaging + docs links; add i18n-ready fields
author: Brian Murphy
release_notes:
- Hosted/Dedicated: residency enforcement errors now include actionable remediation guidance and stable docs links.
- Console/SDKs: added localization-ready error fields (i18n key + args) for consistent rendering.
description:
Context: As we roll out hosted data residency enforcement, Support and pilot customers reported that RESIDENCY_* errors were technically correct but not actionable. In particular, users weren’t sure whether to change the base URL, the SDK region hint, or the org/project pinning settings. This PR updates the error payload contract to include (1) clearer copy, (2) a stable docs link, and (3) i18n-ready fields so Console can render localized messaging without the API having to ship translated strings.

Scope:
- Update error message copy for residency enforcement denials (gateway admission + router constraint failures).
- Add error.docs_url to residency errors (stable, versionless URLs anchored in docs site).
- Add error.i18n_key + error.i18n_args for localization-ready UI surfaces.
- Keep backward compatibility: existing error.code and error.message remain present; new fields are additive.

API contract changes (additive):
- error.docs_url: string (e.g., https://docs.redwoodinference.com/security/data-residency#troubleshooting)
- error.user_message: string (human-friendly summary intended for end-users; safe to show)
- error.remediation: string (short “next step” guidance; safe to show)
- error.i18n_key: string (stable identifier; Console/SDKs can map to localized templates)
- error.i18n_args: map-like object serialized as JSON string at the edge (values are scalars only; no nested objects)

Example payload (RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH):
{
  "error": {
    "code": "RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH",
    "message": "Request was sent to region us-east but your org is pinned to eu-west.",
    "user_message": "This organization only allows requests in EU (eu-west).",
    "remediation": "Use the EU base URL or configure your SDK client for eu-west.",
    "docs_url": "https://docs.redwoodinference.com/security/data-residency#region-mismatch",
    "i18n_key": "errors.residency.region_mismatch",
    "i18n_args": "{\"request_region\":\"us-east\",\"pinned_region\":\"eu-west\"}",
    "request_id": "req_01HP..."
  }
}

Notes:
- We intentionally do not include the full allowed_regions list in user_message by default to avoid leaking policy details across some shared environments; the server-side logs/audit events contain full evaluation context.
- docs_url is stable and should not include query params; anchor fragments are allowed.
- i18n fields are namespaced under errors.residency.* and should be treated as API-stable once GA.

Testing:
- Added unit tests for new fields + snapshot tests for the primary residency codes.
- Updated integration tests to assert docs_url presence and i18n_key stability.

Follow-ups:
- Console: wire i18n_key/i18n_args into the error banner + settings page “Recent violations” table (tracked in ENG-2846).
- Docs: ensure anchors remain stable before GA; Elliot/Docs team to confirm final URLs (tracked in redwood-docs PR separately).

Screenshots: N/A (API-only changes).
commits: api/errors: add user_message/remediation/docs_url fields for residency errors
api/errors: add i18n_key + i18n_args and stabilize keys for RESIDENCY_* codes
gateway: propagate request_region/pinned_region into error context (sanitized)
tests: update residency error snapshots + integration assertions
docs-links: centralize residency docs URL constants
review_conversation: Naomi Feldman: Can we make the remediation text explicit about *which* base URL to use? Customers keep mixing the control plane endpoint and the inference endpoint.

Brian Murphy (author): Good call. I added “Use the EU base URL” language plus a short hint to check SDK config. I avoided hardcoding the exact hostname since we have multi-domain setups; docs_url points to the canonical mapping table.
Chloe Martin: For Console localization, can we rely on error.message being English and render that? Or should Console strictly use i18n_key/user_message?

Brian Murphy (author): Recommendation is Console uses user_message for default and i18n_key/i18n_args when localization is enabled. error.message is still the developer-centric string primarily for logs/debugging and may be more variable over time.
Monica Patel: SDKs currently surface error.message. Adding user_message is great, but do we guarantee it’s safe for display (no secrets)?

Brian Murphy (author): Yes—user_message/remediation are explicitly curated and must be safe to show. I added a short comment in the schema + tests to keep us honest. Full evaluation details remain in audit logs and internal traces.
Amara Diallo: gateway middleware currently sets HTTP 403 for mismatch; is that still correct? Some clients expect 409 for policy conflicts.

Brian Murphy (author): Kept existing status codes unchanged in this PR to avoid breaking behavior during beta. We can revisit in the error-code taxonomy doc after GA; adding fields is already a noticeable improvement.
Elliot Price: Please confirm the docs_url anchors are stable and won’t break when we restructure the docs nav.

Brian Murphy (author): URLs are centralized in packages/common/src/docs/links.ts with tests to prevent accidental changes. Anchors were aligned with the docs PR draft; we’ll update constants if Docs requests a different final anchor before GA.
